summary: Elke Rogersdotter specializes in archaeology and Indology. She earned her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006), where she was supervised by Thomas B. Larsson and Bozena Werbart, with Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad serving as co-advisors.
Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. She was affiliated with Leiden University, where her posts are attested in 2003 and in 2018 as a member of the Editorial Board.
Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a PhD candidate until 1988 and earned his PhD in 1998.

Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a Tibetologist and historian. Educated at Queens College, CUNY, and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn Struve, he served on the faculty at Indiana University (1987–2015) and held posts at Harvard and Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. Her academic appointments include Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).
Emanuela Garatti is a scholar of Tibetology who has held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held positions as a Pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library and Research Institute, at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937), and at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita is an archaeology and art history scholar. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, holding posts at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State.
Emil Krebs (1867–1930) was a linguist and Sinologist. He studied at the University of Breslau and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he was taught by Wilhelm Grube from approximately 1887 to 1890.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a linguist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at Halle (associate in 1830, full 1835–1860) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1860).

Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who was tutored by Franz Joseph Lauth. In 1864, he became a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist, linguist, and Central Asian studies scholar. After studying at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Göttingen under Weber, Kuhn, and Kielhorn, he held chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University, and Göttingen.

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Anton Boller. He served as professor at the universities of Bologna (1860), Pisa (~1861–1885), and Padua (~1888–1912), and worked at the Laurentian and Marciana libraries.

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who earned degrees from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She joined the faculty of the University of Colorado around 2003.

Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who was educated at Somerville College, Oxford, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She has held professorships at the University of Cambridge (~1988) and Harvard University (~2008).

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, completing her PhD under Jan Gonda. She was associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht (1964–1988) and taught at Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Dhaka and Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and held leadership roles at the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art and ICOM.

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities. He served on the faculty at Kyushu University (1941–1980), as professor at Kumamoto University (~1977–1982), and directed the Kyushu Historical Museum.

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held professorships at Nihon Fukushi University, Minobusan University (serving as president 1998–2001), and Rissho University (1972–1997).
Eng Jin Ooi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD at Mahidol University (2021). His doctoral supervisors were Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.
